glosses: Any of various deciduous trees or shrubs in the genus Salix, in the willow family Salicaceae, found primarily on moist soils in cooler zones in the northern hemisphere.

examples.text: […] and through the middle of this forest, from wall to wall, ran a winding line of brilliant green which marked the course of cottonwoods and willows.
And willows, willow-herb, and grass, / And meadowsweet, and haycocks dry, / No whit less still and lonely fair / Than the high cloudlets in the sky.
The pounded leaves of the willow, drunk in a concoction, were formerly reputed to diminish amatory desires.
By old age she was emaciated, the bones jutting out of her face and her figure frail as a willow branch.

glosses: The wood of these trees.
A cricket bat.
The baseball bat.
A rotating spiked drum used to open and clean cotton heads.
To open and cleanse (cotton, flax, wool, etc.) by means of a willow.
To form a shape or move in a way similar to the long, slender branches of a willow.

examples.text: Willowing over the rough cobbles of the little pier stepped a thin, bent figure, adorned with a silver nanny-goat's beard and bobbling eyes interrupted by the rim of a pair of pince-nez.
